Let's verify Kipchoge's marathon records: 1) World Record: 2:01:09 (set at 2022 Berlin Marathon, breaking his previous world record 2:01:39 set in 2018 Berlin Marathon). 2) Unofficial / exhibition (Ineos 1:59 Challenge): 1:59:40 (Vienna 2019). Wait, let's check if there are other possibilities or if the question refers to official world record pace (2:01:09) or 2:01:39 or 1:59:40. Let's calculate the speed and time in hours for all these paces and see how they round to the nearest 1000 hours! Let's test all these calculations in Python: Distance = minimum perigee value on Moon's Wikipedia page. From the Moon page: `| periapsis = {{gaps |362 |600}} km
({{gaps |356 |400}}–{{gaps |370 |400}} km)` Minimum perigee = 356,400 km. (Wait, let's also check if there is any other value in the text like 356,375 or 356,400 or 357,000 km, let's check the prose of Moon's page!). Let's check prose in Moon page: `ranging from {{convert|357000|-|407000|km|mi|sp=us}}` Wait! Let's search the wikitext of Moon page for all occurrences of "35" or "perigee" or "closest" to be 100% sure what values exist on the Wikipedia page! Let's run a script to check all instances of perigee/periapsis and numbers on the Moon page, and do the math for all candidate values of Kipchoge's record marathon pace. ```python cmd = """python3 -c " import urllib.request, json, re headers = {'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0'} req1 = urllib.request.Request('https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=Moon&prop=wikitext&format=json', headers=headers) data1 = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req1).read().decode()) wt1 = data1['parse']['wikitext']['*'] matches = re.findall(r'.{0,50}(?:perigee|periapsis|356|357).{0,50}', wt1, re.IGNORECASE) for m in matches: print(m.strip()) " """ out = await run_command(cmd) print(out) ```
